source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 7 (i)-(iv): properties of the cross product from the definition (book p.283); (i) printed with a garbled symbol. Proofs, no key answer.

blocks.prompt: 7 (i) Use the definition of cross product, for any vectors \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\) and scalar \(k\), prove that \(\underline{u} \times (-\underline{u}) = \underline{0}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh definition se proof (saboot) ka sawal hai.
Dikhana hai ke kisi vector ka us ke ulte (negative) vector ke saath cross product zero vector hai.
Plan: \(\underline{u}\) aur \(-\underline{u}\) ka angle nikalein aur definition mein rakh dein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: koi bhi vector \(\underline{u}\).
Saabit karna hai: \(\underline{u} \times (-\underline{u}) = \underline{0}\).
Tareeqa: Cross product ki definition (14.3.1)
\[\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta\,\hat{n}\]
yahan \(\theta\) dono vectors ka angle hai aur \(\hat{n}\) woh unit vector jo right hand rule se milta hai. Sawal kehta hai "definition use karein", is liye components nahi, yahi formula lagayenge.

Jab \(\underline{u} = \underline{0}\) ho
\[\underline{0} \times \underline{0} = \underline{0}\]
Kyun: Agar koi vector zero ho to formula mein \(|\underline{u}| = 0\) aa jata hai aur poora product zero ho jata hai. Yeh aasaan case alag kar diya; ab hum \(\underline{u} \ne \underline{0}\) maan kar chalte hain.

\(\underline{u}\) aur \(-\underline{u}\) ka angle
\[\theta = \pi, \quad \sin\pi = 0\]
\[|-\underline{u}| = |\underline{u}|\]
Kyun: \(-\underline{u}\) ki lambai \(\underline{u}\) jitni hi hai lekin rukh bilkul ulta hai. Misaal: ek banda mashriq (east) ki taraf aur doosra maghrib (west) ki taraf chale to un ke raaston ke darmiyan \(180^{\circ}\) ka angle hai.

Definition mein rakhein
\[\underline{u} \times (-\underline{u}) = |\underline{u}||-\underline{u}|\sin\pi\,\hat{n}\]
\[= |\underline{u}|^2(0)\,\hat{n} = \underline{0}\]
Kyun: Lambai wale hisse mein \(\sin\pi = 0\) aa gaya, to product ki lambai zero hai, aur jis vector ki lambai zero ho woh zero vector hai, rukh chahe kuch bhi ho.
Dhyan dein: Jawab \(\underline{0}\) (zero vector) likhein, sirf 0 nahi, kyunke cross product hamesha vector hota hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: 7 (i) mein kitab ne left side ka doosra vector ek bigde hue nishaan ke saath chhapa hai aur right side par sirf 0 likha hai. Sahi statement \(\underline{u} \times (-\underline{u}) = \underline{0}\) hai, yani jawab zero vector hai.

blocks.prompt: 7 (ii) Use the definition of cross product, for any vectors \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\) and scalar \(k\), prove that \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = -\underline{v} \times \underline{u}\).
blocks.explanation:
Definition se proof.
Dikhana hai ke tarteeb badalne se sirf sign badalta hai, lambai nahi.
Plan: pehle lambaiyan compare karein, phir right hand rule se rukh (direction).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: koi bhi do vectors \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), jin ka angle \(\theta\) hai.
Saabit karna hai: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = -(\underline{v} \times \underline{u})\).
Tareeqa: Definition \[\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta\,\hat{n}\]
Koi bhi vector do cheezon se pehchana jata hai: lambai aur rukh. Dono ko alag alag compare karenge.

Lambaiyan compare karein
\[|\underline{u} \times \underline{v}| = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta\]
\[= |\underline{v}||\underline{u}|\sin\theta = |\underline{v} \times \underline{u}|\]
Kyun: Do vectors ka angle wohi \(\theta\) rehta hai chahe pehle kisi ko bhi likhein, aur \(|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\) aam numbers ka product hai jis mein tarteeb se farq nahi padta.

Rukh compare karein
\[\underline{u} \times \underline{v}:\ \hat{n}, \qquad \underline{v} \times \underline{u}:\ -\hat{n}\]
Kyun: Right hand rule: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) mein daayen haath ki ungliyan \(\underline{u}\) se \(\underline{v}\) ki taraf modte hain to angootha \(\hat{n}\) deta hai. \(\underline{v} \times \underline{u}\) mein ungliyan ulti taraf mudti hain, is liye angootha neeche, yani \(-\hat{n}\). Misaal: pench (screw) ko ek taraf ghumayein to andar jata hai, ulta ghumayein to bahar aata hai.

Lambai aur rukh ko jor dein
\[\underline{v} \times \underline{u} = |\underline{v}||\underline{u}|\sin\theta\,(-\hat{n})\]
\[= -\left(|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta\,\hat{n}\right)\]
\[= -(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\]
Kyun: Lambai same, rukh ulta, to ek doosre ka negative. Dono taraf \(-1\) se multiply karein to \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = -(\underline{v} \times \underline{u})\). Agar koi vector zero ho to dono taraf \(\underline{0}\) hai, wahan bhi sahi.
Dhyan dein: Is liye cross product mein vectors ki jagah kabhi bina sign badle mat badlein.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = -\underline{v} \times \underline{u}\) (cross product anti-commutative hai)

blocks.prompt: 7 (iii) Use the definition of cross product, for any vectors \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\) and scalar \(k\), prove that \(\underline{u} \times (k\underline{v}) = (k\underline{u}) \times \underline{v} = k(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\).
blocks.explanation:
Definition se proof, lekin \(k\) ke sign ke hisaab se alag alag cases banenge.
Dikhana hai ke scalar (number) kisi bhi vector se nikal kar bahar aa sakta hai.
Plan: \(k > 0\), \(k = 0\), \(k < 0\) ke cases; phir part (ii) ki madad se \((k\underline{u}) \times \underline{v}\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: vectors \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}\) jin ka angle \(\theta\) hai aur \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta\,\hat{n}\); aur ek scalar \(k\).
Saabit karna hai: \(\underline{u} \times (k\underline{v}) = (k\underline{u}) \times \underline{v} = k(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\).
Tareeqa: \(\underline{v}\) ko \(k\) se multiply karne se us ki lambai \(|k||\underline{v}|\) ho jati hai, aur agar \(k\) negative ho to us ka rukh bhi ulta ho jata hai. Hum dekhenge ke is se angle aur \(\hat{n}\) par kya asar hota hai. Cases is liye banane parte hain ke negative \(k\) rukh badal deta hai.

Case \(k > 0\)
\[\underline{u} \times (k\underline{v}) = |\underline{u}|\,(k|\underline{v}|)\sin\theta\,\hat{n}\]
\[= k(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\]
Kyun: Positive \(k\) se \(\underline{v}\) sirf lamba ya chhota hota hai, rukh wohi rehta hai. Is liye angle \(\theta\) aur \(\hat{n}\) wohi, bas lambai \(k\) guna. Misaal: \(k = 2\) ho to parallelogram ki ek side dugni, area bhi dugna.

Case \(k = 0\)
\[\underline{u} \times (0\underline{v}) = \underline{u} \times \underline{0} = \underline{0}\]
\[0(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}) = \underline{0}\]
Kyun: Dono taraf zero vector aata hai, to barabar hain.

Case \(k < 0\)
\[\underline{u} \times (k\underline{v}) = |\underline{u}|(-k)|\underline{v}|\sin(\pi - \theta)(-\hat{n})\]
\[= k\,|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta\,\hat{n}\]
\[= k(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\]
Kyun: Negative \(k\) se \(k\underline{v}\) ulti taraf mud jata hai. Us ki lambai \(|k||\underline{v}| = -k|\underline{v}|\) hai (kyunke \(k\) negative hai to \(-k\) positive). \(\underline{u}\) ke saath angle ab \(\pi - \theta\) hai, aur right hand rule rukh \(-\hat{n}\) deta hai. Ab \(\sin(\pi - \theta) = \sin\theta\) aur \((-k)(-\hat{n}) = k\hat{n}\), yani do minus mil kar plus.
Dhyan dein: Lambai kabhi negative nahi hoti, is liye \(k|\underline{v}|\) nahi, \(-k|\underline{v}|\) likha.

Ab \((k\underline{u}) \times \underline{v}\)
\[(k\underline{u}) \times \underline{v} = -\big(\underline{v} \times (k\underline{u})\big)\]
\[= -k(\underline{v} \times \underline{u})\]
\[= -k\big(-(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\big) = k(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\]
Kyun: Teen cases dobara karne ke bajaye chhota rasta: part (ii) se tarteeb badli, upar wala result (jo kisi bhi do vectors ke liye sahi hai) laga kar \(k\) bahar nikala, aur part (ii) se tarteeb wapas kar di. Do minus plus ban gaye.

Natija (conclusion)
\[\underline{u} \times (k\underline{v}) = (k\underline{u}) \times \underline{v} = k(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\]
Kyun: Dono products \(k(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\) ke barabar nikle, to teenon barabar hain. Matlab: number kisi bhi vector ke saath ho, cross product se bahar aa sakta hai.

blocks.prompt: 7 (iv) Use the definition of cross product, for any vectors \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\) and scalar \(k\), prove that \(\underline{u} \times (\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = (\underline{u} \times \underline{v}) + (\underline{u} \times \underline{w})\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh distributive law (taqseemi qanoon) hai, aur definition se saabit karna hai; yeh is sawal ka sab se mushkil hissa hai, aaram se parhiye.
Dikhana hai ke \(\underline{u} \times\) jama (sum) par baant-ta hai.
Plan: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{x}\) ko teen aasaan kaamon (saya lena, ghumana, lamba karna) se banayenge; har kaam jama ko jama hi rehne deta hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: koi bhi vectors \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}, \underline{w}\).
Saabit karna hai: \(\underline{u} \times (\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = \underline{u} \times \underline{v} + \underline{u} \times \underline{w}\).
Tareeqa: Agar \(\underline{u} = \underline{0}\) ho to dono taraf \(\underline{0}\). Warna \(\Pi\) woh plane (hamwar satah) lein jo \(O\) se guzarta hai aur \(\underline{u}\) par perpendicular hai; socho \(\underline{u}\) ek khamba hai jo farsh \(\Pi\) par seedha khada hai. Hum dikhayenge ke kisi bhi vector \(\underline{x}\) se \(\underline{u} \times \underline{x}\) teen aise kaamon se banta hai jo jama ko jama mein badalte hain.

Teen kaam jo \(\underline{u} \times \underline{x}\) banate hain
\[\underline{x} \to \underline{x}' \to \underline{x}'' \to |\underline{u}|\,\underline{x}''\]
Kyun: (1) \(\underline{x}'\) = \(\underline{x}\) ka farsh \(\Pi\) par saya (projection), jaise khambe ki seedh mein roshni daalein to vector ka saya farsh par girta hai; is ki lambai \(|\underline{x}|\sin\theta\) hai. (2) \(\underline{x}''\) = is saye ko farsh par hi \(90^{\circ}\) ghuma dein (khambe ki choti se dekhein to ghari ki sui ke ulat); ab yeh right hand rule wale \(\hat{n}\) ki taraf hai aur lambai wohi \(|\underline{x}|\sin\theta\). (3) \(|\underline{u}|\) se multiply karein. Natija: lambai \(|\underline{u}||\underline{x}|\sin\theta\) aur rukh \(\hat{n}\), yani bilkul \(\underline{u} \times \underline{x}\).

Har kaam jama ko jama rakhta hai
\[(\underline{v} + \underline{w})' = \underline{v}' + \underline{w}'\]
\[(\underline{v}' + \underline{w}')'' = \underline{v}'' + \underline{w}''\]
\[|\underline{u}|(\underline{v}'' + \underline{w}'') = |\underline{u}|\underline{v}'' + |\underline{u}|\underline{w}''\]
Kyun: \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\) aur \(\underline{v} + \underline{w}\) ek triangle banate hain; us triangle ka saya bhi triangle hota hai, is liye jama ka saya = sayon ka jama. Poore triangle ko \(90^{\circ}\) ghumayein to woh triangle hi rehta hai, is liye jama ko ghumana = ghumaye hue vectors ka jama. Aur kisi number se multiply karna jama par baant-ta hai, yeh to hum jaante hain.

Teenon kaam jor dein
\[\underline{u} \times (\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = |\underline{u}|(\underline{v} + \underline{w})''\]
\[= |\underline{u}|\underline{v}'' + |\underline{u}|\underline{w}''\]
\[= \underline{u} \times \underline{v} + \underline{u} \times \underline{w}\]
Kyun: Pehle step 2 ko \(\underline{v} + \underline{w}\) par lagaya, phir step 3, phir step 2 ko \(\underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) par alag alag. Yahi saboot hai.

Ek misaal se tasdeeq
\[\underline{u} = \underline{i},\ \underline{v} = \underline{j},\ \underline{w} = \underline{k}\]
\[\underline{i} \times (\underline{j} + \underline{k}) = \underline{k} - \underline{j}\]
\[\underline{i} \times \underline{j} + \underline{i} \times \underline{k} = \underline{k} - \underline{j}\]
Kyun: \(\underline{i} \times \underline{j} = \underline{k}\) aur \(\underline{i} \times \underline{k} = -\underline{j}\) (cyclic order ka ulta, is liye minus); left side determinant se bhi \(\underline{k} - \underline{j}\) aata hai. Dono barabar, to qanoon is misaal par bhi chalta hai. Yaad rahe: misaal saboot nahi, sirf tasalli hai; saboot upar wale steps hain.
